name: Starprint
tagline: White pencil on coloured paper, hand-drawn
lineage: Grew up as Bureau's Starry Sidekick and was called Starful Gothic here. Gothic is now one of the papers rather than the whole thing.
story: A drawing done in white pencil, printed on whatever paper was in the drawer. The line is always the same hand — loose, unhurried, a little wobbly where it was drawn fast — and the paper is what changes: black for Gothic, a deep hedge green for Labyrinth, a night-sea blue for Skysea. Autumn is the odd one, printed the other way round: brown ink on tan stock, because you cannot print white on paper that pale. Stars are scattered across all of them, and they are drawn rather than rendered.
principles: One hand, several papers — the drawing never changes, only what it is printed on.
The line is the ink and the ink is the drawing: no fills, no shadows, nothing solid.
A star is drawn, not lit. Scatter them unevenly; a regular sky is a rendered sky.
Every paper carries its own ink, which is why Autumn prints dark and the rest print pale.
do: Outline surfaces in the near-opaque white line.
Scatter stars in empty space — they are punctuation, not wallpaper.
Let headings feel hand-lettered: a humanist face, generously sized.
dont: No box-shadows, ever — and never the value none where a shadow composes; write a zero shadow.
No filled white surfaces; white is for lines and text only.
No third accent colour, however tempting.

voice.tone: Playful but quiet, like notes traded after midnight. It can joke; it never shouts.

display.stack: Optima, 'Gill Sans', 'Gill Sans MT', 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', sans-serif

body.stack: Optima, 'Gill Sans', 'Gill Sans MT', 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', sans-serif

motion.character: Drift, not snap — things move the way slow constellations do.

texture.notes: Star-speckled night checker. Future asset hook: the site's hand-drawn GIFs (persona, sun, cassettes) as optional ornaments.

notes: Seeded from Bureau's Starry Sidekick. Gothic is the committed original and the other three papers are first guesses — Timothy named the colours, the hexes are mine. Autumn is read as a genuinely light paper, so it inverts: dark ink on tan. If it was meant as a dark warm brown alongside the others, that is a one-variant change. Each variant carries its own backdrop colours, because the stars are drawn in the ink of that printing.
